original_value: We introduce a mean field game with rank-based reward: competing agents optimize their effort to achieve a goal, are ranked according to their completion time, and are paid a reward based on their relative rank. First, we propose a tractable Poissonian model in which we can describe the optimal effort for a given reward scheme. Second, we study the principal–agent problem of designing an optimal reward scheme. A surprising, explicit design is found to minimize the time until a given fraction of the population has reached the goal.

result.paraphrase: We introduce a mean field game with rank-based rewards: agents compete by choosing effort to reach a target, are ordered by completion time, and receive payment according to their relative rank. First, we present a tractable Poissonian model that lets us characterize the optimal effort under a given reward scheme. Second, we analyze the principal–agent problem of constructing an optimal reward scheme. We obtain a surprising explicit design that minimizes the time needed for a given fraction of the population to reach the goal.
